messages:
Sam (sales): Quick sync — AureliaHealth POC: they require their DMZ TLS inspector to see SNI and also want the original client IP in app logs. Which network path should we recommend for the POC (peering vs PrivateLink)?

Aria (solutions): Short answer: VPC peering preserves client source IP and lets their inline inspector see SNI without extra proxies. PrivateLink isolates traffic (no route sharing) but hides client IP behind endpoint ENIs unless the customer terminates TLS and re-TLS to us or inserts X-Forwarded-For.

Ravi (netops): Two quick options:
- Peering: TGW -> spoke -> peering -> redwood-vpc (no NAT) => client IP preserved, SNI visible to their inspector.
- PrivateLink: TGW -> spoke -> interface endpoint -> ENI -> redwood (src becomes endpoint IP).

Clara (security): For their security questionnaire: we support mTLS, customer-managed KMS/HSM integration, audit logs exportable to S3/SIEM, and key rotation. Note: if they require in-line TLS inspection, they must terminate TLS in their DMZ and re-establish TLS to Redwood.

Sam (sales): They also asked for a quick cost delta for ~5TB/mo to include in the SOW. Ballpark numbers?

Ravi (netops): Ballpark: PrivateLink infra = endpoint hourly (~$0.01/hr) + data processing (~$0.01/GB) => ~ $50-70/mo for 5TB (ex cloud egress). Peering: no endpoint fees, cross-VPC transfer varies ($0.005-$0.02/GB) => ~$25-$100/mo. Peering often cheaper at scale but needs route/peering approval.

Aria (solutions): SOW blurb (one-paragraph): "Recommendation: For AureliaHealths POC, we recommend VPC peering when both SNI visibility to a customer TLS inspector and preservation of original client IP are required. Peering preserves source IPs and allows the customers DMZ to observe SNI without terminating/injecting TLS proxies. If the customer forbids cross-account peering, PrivateLink is an alternative but requires TLS termination on the customer side or a proxy that forwards X-Forwarded-For, and carries modest per-GB interface processing fees."

Sam (sales): Paste-ready firewall allowlist lines for customer ops?

Ravi (netops): Snippet to hand to Aurelia ops:
```
# PrivateLink (interface endpoint)
Allow TCP/443 -> <interface-endpoint-subnet-cidrs>
Allow TCP/443 -> <redwood-controlplane-ips>  # only if instructed

# VPC Peering
Allow TCP/443 -> <redwood-peering-cidr>

# Common
Enforce TLS 1.2+; deny legacy ciphers
Log X-Forwarded-For if using proxy termination
```

Clara (security): Also flag: if they want both SNI inspection and native client-ip preservation without any header plumbing, mark as MUST use peering. We'll include KMS/HSM wording in questionnaire response.

ticket-bot: Created RW-4120: "AureliaHealth POC - network decision & cost delta" and linked a short runbook template.

Sam (sales): Thanks everyone — I'll capture choices in the SOW and ask Aurelia which path they prefer. Will follow up once they reply. :thumbsup:
